record.question: The first country in the world who use Facial Recognition for paying taxes is
record.explanation: For the November 2020 paper, Singapore is the intended country: SingPass Face Verification was introduced in July 2020 and was being used for access to tax services. Contemporary coverage explicitly described this as the first national scheme for paying taxes through facial verification: https://www.indiatimes.com/news/world/singapore-is-the-first-nation-using-facial-recognition-for-paying-taxes/articleshow/127669216.html ; the July launch is confirmed by GovTech: https://www.tech.gov.sg/media/2020-11-04-sign-with-singpass/ .

record.question: The Mizo idiom 'Mahni malchunga sa chan' means
record.explanation: Tentatively, the idiom conveys selfishness or acting for one's own benefit, matching Mahni hmasial. Its literal image is slicing meat in one's own lap, documented in the bibliography at https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/mizo-discovery-of-the-british-raj/bibliography/80FBC512EFECC155B83F68A5458D75AA ; however, I could not verify an authoritative idiomatic gloss, so this remains a low-confidence inference requiring review.

record.question: In the traditional Mizo wedding, as part of a subsidiary bride price, 'Naupuakpuan' is given to
record.explanation: Naupuakpuan is the subsidiary marriage-price share given to the bride's elder sister in recognition of caring for her as a baby. Schedule II, explanation 6, of the 2014 Mizo Marriage, Divorce and Inheritance of Property Act states this explicitly: https://printingstationery.mizoram.gov.in/storage/site/files/gazette_1780_54b7841549c39.pdf .

record.question: 'Tuha kuai rual' in Mizo demographic division refers to which of the following groups?
record.explanation: Tuha kuai rual denotes adolescent girls old enough to begin agricultural work. SCERT defines it as Hmeichhe tleirawl in https://scert.mizoram.gov.in/uploads/attachments/f04935376f4ed1602c181b7a31957111/kumtluang-8.pdf ; the traditional age classification specifies girls around 14–17 at https://tinghleithang.blogspot.com/2012/10/mizo-history.html .
